titel: Am I a Bad Person, For Not Wanting To Help My Mother-in-Law?

einzeiler: Financial advice on market volatility, layoffs, estate planning, and Social Security.
kurzfassung: Suze Orman and KT answer listener questions covering topics like stock market volatility and the rule of 55 for layoffs. They also discuss services for childfree estate planning, inherited traditional IRAs, and whether to financially support aging family members. Finally, they address concerns regarding the long-term solvency of Social Security.
stichpunkte: The stock market is expected to experience a rough patch around late August into September, presenting dollar-cost averaging opportunities.
Employees who leave their job in the year they turn 55 can use the 55 rule to withdraw from a 401k without a 10% penalty.
Childfree trust management services can incur high annual and hourly fees, making personal arrangements or professional trustees a potentially better alternative.
The 10-year rule to wipe clean an inherited retirement account under the Secure Act generally applies only to deaths occurring in 2020 or later.
Supporting elderly family members involves balancing personal financial boundaries with compassionate family responsibilities.
Social Security cannot borrow money, meaning benefits automatically adjust to incoming revenue if reserves deplete and Congress takes no action.

clips.text: Rachel, 55, seeks guidance on transferring her 401k after unexpectedly re-entering the workforce.

clips.hook: The hidden costs of childfree trust services
clips.text: The host warns against using third-party services for end-of-life planning, arguing that strangers lack the necessary personal insight to make critical decisions.

clips.hook: Inherited IRA rules and the Secure Act
clips.text: A grandmother asks for clarification on the ten-year withdrawal rule for an inherited IRA she received from her mother in 2016.
